finding.abuseipdb.reported: AbuseIPDB: the server's IP address has an abuse confidence score of {score}% ({reports} report(s) from {users} user(s) over 90 days).
module.abuseipdb.checks: Queries AbuseIPDB for the target's IP address: abuse confidence score, number of reports over the last 90 days, usage type, provider and country.
module.abuseipdb.fix:
Open the address's page on AbuseIPDB (`abuseipdb.com/check/203.0.113.10`): read the report categories (SSH brute force, port scan, spam, phishing, web attack...), the dates and the comments. They show what the machine did.
If the address is yours, treat the server as possibly compromised: isolate it if needed, examine the logs (authentication, web server, mail) for the dates quoted, look for unknown accounts, SSH keys, processes and scheduled tasks, then clean it or rebuild it from a clean image.
Change the passwords, SSH keys and API tokens that may have leaked, update the system and applications, and close needlessly exposed services at the firewall (SSH, RDP, databases, administration interfaces) or restrict them to allowed addresses.
If the address is shared (shared hosting, corporate NAT, VPN, reassigned address), the source may be another machine: identify it with the firewall or NAT logs, or ask the host to deal with the abuse or to give you another address.
Let the score come down: the weight of reports decreases over time and the rating is recalculated every day, provided there is no new abuse. The module looks at the last 90 days.
If reports are wrong or concern a former use of the address, a registered user can file a takedown request ("Takedown Request") from the address's page on AbuseIPDB, with evidence. Do not contact support to have a report deleted.
Check the score with the command in the snippet (`abuseConfidenceScore` field), then run the DomainRecon scan again; the result is cached for 24 hours.
module.abuseipdb.fix_snippet:
# curl
curl -G https://api.abuseipdb.com/api/v2/check --data-urlencode "ipAddress=203.0.113.10" -d maxAgeInDays=90 -H "Key: $ABUSEIPDB_KEY" -H "Accept: application/json"
# PowerShell
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.abuseipdb.com/api/v2/check?ipAddress=203.0.113.10&maxAgeInDays=90" -Headers @{ Key = $env:ABUSEIPDB_KEY; Accept = "application/json" }
module.abuseipdb.title: AbuseIPDB reputation
module.abuseipdb.why: An IP address reported for attacks or spam is often blocked by firewalls and mail servers: it reveals a compromised server or a poorly chosen address.
